author: Judith Ritholz
text:
The needles are supposed to be long. They need to go through the skin into the subcutaneous (below the skin) level to sample the interstitial (space between the cells) fluid. It's the same space that many vaccines are given and where are insulin using diabetics inject themselves. It seems unlikely you got three bad sensors. Perhaps you need to fine-tune your application technique. If the tissue of your arm is shifting while you're pressing down, the needle won't go straight in so either it won't end up deep enough or if it shifts enough, you can actually flatten the needle sideways and get no penetration. Presuming you're putting it on the back of your arm, I'd suggest that you need to stretch the tissue as much as possible to get a tight surface moving your arm across your chest while also bending your elbow as much as possible.  Look in a mirror while you're doing this if you're not. Talk to whoever prescribed this for you if it gets confusing.

Best,
MD and fellow user
